messages:
emily_docs: heads-up — we had a few docs PRs pile up this morning blocked on approvals + preview timing. question: can we make a clear rule for trivial doc fixes so they don't wait for the full CODEOWNERS queue?

sam_engineer: can you give examples of 'trivial'? link fixes, grammar, tiny API example tweak? :thinking_face:

emily_docs: yeah exactly — link fixes, single-line typo, or a 1-sentence clarifying note. nothing that changes behavior or examples.

anjali_pm: from product side — we prefer at least one eyes on things that mention product changes, but for pure docs-only typos i'd be fine with a fast-track.

sam_engineer: technically github branch protection can require CODEOWNERS review. auto-merge + "require status checks" still works if approvals are satisfied. problem is: bots like dependabot or docs-bot won't get CODEOWNER approval automatically.

oliver_release: we should also avoid merges during the 30m before releases — it creates noise for release checks. proposing a 1hr daily merge window: 11:00–12:00 PST for non-urgent docs merges.

ci-bot: build started for PR #4217 (docs/link-fix). preview: https://docs-preview.corp/preview/4217 — checks: lint: ✅, build: ✅, preview: ✅

emily_docs: nice. so suggested policy:
- trivial docs PRs (label: docs/trivial) auto-merge when all CI checks pass and docs-preview is green.
- non-trivial PRs: need 1 CODEOWNER approval + CI.
- all merges happen in daily window by default, unless explicitly marked urgent.

sam_engineer: sounds OK. one caveat: CODEOWNERS may be set to require multiple approvers for some folders. we could update CODEOWNERS to map docs/* to @redwood/docs-owners (single group) so a single approval suffices.

emily_docs: any objections to adding a docs owners team?

anjali_pm: fine by PMs. agree that a single-team owner is easier.

sam_engineer: also, GitHub has a setting: "Allow auto-merge" + "Require approvals". We can allow auto-merge for PRs with the docs/trivial label by adding a small GitHub Action that applies the label automatically for quick changes from the docs team. Example snippet:
```yaml
# .github/workflows/label-trivial.yml
name: label-trivial-docs
on: pull_request
jobs:
  detect-trivial:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: quick diff check
        run: |
          git fetch origin ${{ github.base_ref }}
          CHANGES=$(git diff --name-only origin/${{ github.base_ref }}...${{ github.sha }})
          if echo "$CHANGES" | grep -E "^docs/.*\.(md|mdx)$" >/dev/null && [ $(echo "$CHANGES" | wc -l) -le 2 ]; then
            gh pr edit ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} --add-label docs/trivial
          fi
```

oliver_release: careful — gating label-by-diff can be gamed, but ok as a convenience. ops will still monitor merges during window.

docs-bot: docs preview aggregator: PR #4217 preview build succeeded. live preview: https://docs-preview.corp/preview/4217 :white_check_mark:

sam_engineer: another config we should check: repo settings > protection > "Require review from Code Owners" vs "Require approvals". if we keep require code owners, then adding a docs team as owner gives single-person approvals (from that team) enough.

emily_docs: so next steps are: 1) add @redwood/docs-owners to CODEOWNERS for docs/*, 2) add label workflow above, 3) enable auto-merge for PRs with docs/trivial label, 4) ops set scheduled merge window and monitor.

anjali_pm: quick question — who toggles the repo setting for auto-merge? needs admin.

sam_engineer: I can do that but will coordinate with security to ensure branch protection remains consistent. I’ll open an infra change PR.

oliver_release: ops will watch the first week and report any unwanted merges. if anything odd, we flip the auto-merge off.

emily_docs: thanks — can we target rollout by tomorrow morning? small change, low risk.

sam_engineer: yep. filing infra PR now and will ping here when it's merged.

ci-bot: infra PR #1023 opened by @sam_engineer for branch-protection/docs-auto-merge

emily_docs: sweet. thanks everyone :party_parrot:
